props.name: risk-statement
props.value: Failure to deploy services across multiple availability zones increases the risk of extended service outages due to a single point of failure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Deploy the system in {{ insert: param, rs-1_prm_1 }} availability zones (AZs) within the region.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Utilise cloud-native services for load-balancing and auto-scaling across multiple AZs. Implement health checks and automated failover mechanisms to redirect traffic. Ensure data is replicated across multiple AZs.

guidelines.prose: The number of availability zones to deploy to.

props.name: risk-statement
props.value: Failure to implement dynamic resource scaling may lead to inefficient resource utilisation and potential service degradation during spikes in demand. This can lead to system outages during peak loads, reducing overall system performance and reliability.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Implement and utilise dynamic resource scaling techniques in the system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose:
Resource optimisation techniques such as load balancing and auto-scaling should be employed to maximise resource utilisation and minimise idle resources by adjusting to real-time demand fluctuations.
Refer to the AWS Well-Architected Framework's 'Reliability' pillar for further guidance on implementing resilient systems.

props.name: risk-statement
props.value: Inadequate load testing may lead to unexpected system failures during periods of high demand, leading to service interruptions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Perform load testing every {{ insert: param, rs-3_prm_1 }} days.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Load testing should be conducted on a replica of the production system. The load should mimic real user traffic.

guidelines.prose: The frequency at which load testing should be performed.
